title: Unfairness
text: “Way to go, bro!”
“That was great. Sakura wanted to help Naofumi, too.”
“Thanks, Keel and Sakura. Well, the vibe here is a little awkward, so I think I’ll call it a night a little early today.”

My Father chatted amiably with Keel and Sakura for a bit before turning to me. There’s no need for me to stay here any longer. On his way out, my Father gave Trash and Crimson Swine a defiant smirk before walking away. That’s right… your schemes have come to a bad end.
“Honestly, seeing how things went, how could anyone think they were forcing us to fight…”
Watching Keel enthusiastically praise the fight that just took place, Ren seems to have realized just how close my Father and Keel are.
“Itsuki seems to have a strong sense of justice, but he tends to ignore reason…”
“That’s certainly true.”
“Motoyasu…”
Ren seems to be averting his gaze for some reason. What’s up with me?
“Naofumi.”
“Hm?”
“You were a weak Shield Class, but I think you put up a good fight. I didn’t expect you to be able to fight like that. You did well.”
“Eh, uh… yeah.”
“Compared to that, Itsuki hasn’t been training hard enough… To lose to a Shield Class, of all people.”
At Ren’s follow-up remark, Father furrowed his brow, looking slightly irritated.
“Big bro is strong, you know!”
“Yeah, Naofumi is strong.”
Keel and Sakura-chan protested to Ren, but Father stopped them. It seemed like he’d had enough of this unnecessary commotion.
“The party’s lost its spark, so let’s head back.”
“You’re right. Well then, we’ll come back to the castle tomorrow.”

After all, there was no telling what might happen inside the castle after this. We left the hall—which was now filled with a deflated atmosphere after losing to Father—with a sense of panache. I heard later that the grumpy Trash and the Crimson Swine went on quite a rampage, but I don’t know anything about that.
The next morning. After resting at an inn outside the castle, we slipped through the castle gates at dawn. We were escorted to the throne room to wait for Trash to arrive.
“At this rate, we won’t be able to abolish slavery…”

Itsuki is still holding a grudge over losing to Father last night and is grumbling incessantly that he didn’t actually lose. Apparently, according to Father, if Itsuki had won, they were planning to move toward abolishing slavery. He said something along the lines of how that would be difficult as long as there are heroes who use slaves.
Because of that, Itsuki is glaring at Father as if he were his sworn enemy. Incidentally, Ren was watching this scene with a look of disgust on his face.

You can’t just forcibly strip my Father of his combat strength, you Trash. Even with Keel and Sakura-chan as they are now—not to mention Yuki-chan and Kou—there’s no way they could win, no matter how many of this castle’s soldiers teamed up against them. Hahaha!

That said, Father has become slightly more on guard. He muttered before going to sleep that, although he’d gotten so annoyed he ended up winning, it might have actually been better to lose on purpose. He said it would be difficult to deal with if they started weaving strange conspiracies or taking actions outside the scope of my knowledge of the future.

There’s a month and a half until the next wave, after all. Considering the timing when Father’s innocence will be proven in the future, it’s crucial to make it look like he’s operating within the country for the next month and a half.
“…Well then, let’s hand out the bounties and aid funds for this wave.”

That Trash sat there arrogantly on the throne, looking at me and my Father as if we were trash, before saying that. His aides brought over the money bags. They seem to vary in size, but at the very least, 500 silver coins are guaranteed.

My Father did say, though, that there’s still a possibility they might pick a fight over yesterday’s incident and confiscate the money. The problem is that any further mistreatment will only accelerate Ren’s distrust toward the country he represents. Well, it does seem like he’s already completely turned his back on it, though.
“Now, to each of the heroes…”
When I checked the bag, it jingled—it looked like there were about 500 silver coins. Father’s was the same. What should I buy with this income?
Given the timing… Filo-tan!

That’s right. Father acquired Filo-tan around this time. Last time, to coincide with this season, I rushed to the Monster Merchant to buy up all of Filolial-sama’s eggs. But I wasn’t able to get any at all.

Now then… what exactly did Father say when he acquired Filo-tan in the future? I think he said he bought her from the Monster Merchant… but the exact details are a bit fuzzy. Did he hear it from the Monster Merchant himself? I’m not entirely sure if I heard it directly from Father’s own mouth.

Either way, timing-wise, it was around this time. Considering the regular customer who bought the slave, the next step is to have Father purchase Filo-tan. I need to ask Father directly and find out what to do if he doesn’t believe anyone.
“First, Lord Itsuki… Your exploits are resonating throughout the nation. You’ve done well to accomplish that difficult task and fight for the country. Here are 7,600 silver coins.”

My Father is staring blankly at Itsuki. 7,600 silver coins! That’s equivalent to 76 gold coins! It’s safe to assume that most of the silver coins I was originally supposed to receive were diverted to Itsuki, and this is on top of that. It’s surely just my Trash Father’s way of harassing me for winning. As proof, he’s jingling a huge gold pouch right in front of us, showing it off.
“You’re not appreciated because you’re doing bad things.”

That really gets on my nerves. I’ve been letting it slide to avoid triggering a loop, but since we’re at it, maybe I’ll just blow off his limbs—just enough so he doesn’t die? You, the Trash who’s backing you, and that Crimson Swine are outlaws with power like the embodiment of evil.
“Next, Lord Ren—as expected, adding your contributions against the waves and the reward for completing my request, that comes to 3,800 silver coins.”
“…Half.”

Ren hasn’t changed much, has he? However, perhaps his suspicion toward the Trash and the Crimson Swine is growing, as he’s quietly accepting the payment. Deep down, he’s probably comparing the amount of work he and Itsuki have done and feeling it’s unfair.

After all, I haven’t heard of any notable feats from Itsuki. To be honest, the only things currently being talked about in Melromarc are the Sword Hero and the Mysterious Saint. Even his companions seem to sense Ren’s bad mood and are hesitating to speak to him.
“Next, Lord Motoyasu… since you don’t seem to have done anything particularly noteworthy, that’ll be 600 silver coins.”
Well, well—it seems my share is a bit on the high side. Well, as far as Trash is concerned, he’s defending my Father, but I suppose he thinks he can somehow pull it off?

Unfortunately, my Father is just stopping him before he goes too far. Depending on the time and circumstances, I’d love to wipe him out, but I’ll have to hold back. Just one and a half more months to endure. It’s unpleasant to see that Crimson Swine flashing a fake smile right next to Trash.
And finally, it’s my father.
“Hmph, I’ll have to make the Shield work a little harder. It’s just the aid money. No, wait—I’m deducting 200 silver coins for the medical expenses after you poisoned Itsuki into unconsciousness.”
…So, my father is saying 300 silver coins? Is this amount being added to Itsuki’s total? This farce has gone too far.
“… 200 silver coins for medical expenses? After forcing him into a fight, this is what we get? Naofumi must have done some work with the waves, right?”

Ren glares at Trash. Ren’s distrust has now surpassed all limits. This is also a dangerous sign. If Ren were to lose control and interfere with Trash or the Three Heroes Church, my knowledge of the future would be useless. Not to mention, Ren alone is no match for the Pope’s weapon.
“From the looks of it, Naofumi and the others don’t seem to be doing any guild work. Do you know anything about this?”
“Um…”
My Father is looking right at me. Jobs like that certainly wouldn’t be handed out based on Trash’s authority. But how should I answer this?

I’ve probably stoked Ren’s suspicion a bit too much. It’s easy to imagine that depending on my answer, things could take a serious turn. If I just went on a rampage right here, I have a feeling Ren would trust us, but on the other hand, my relationship with Itsuki would be completely severed.
It’s a frustrating situation. To begin with… I have a vague feeling that it might already be too late.
“The Guild did exist, but they didn’t arrange any work for us.”
“I see. Well, if it’s a guild in this country, I suppose it can’t be helped…”

But it’s going to be difficult to deceive Ren at this point. If I tell a ridiculous lie, it might render everything we’ve built up so far meaningless. Saying I didn’t even know about the guild would be a stretch, wouldn’t it?

The die has already been cast. I don’t know how things will play out from here, but I have to be somewhat concerned for Ren’s life as well. It’s easy to focus on Itsuki, the tree that caused the loop last time, but we must also protect Ren’s life. If we were to let Ren escape, would Zeltoble be a possibility?

He’s probably being watched, but at this stage, I think Ren can still move about with a certain degree of freedom. Since they’re only suspicious and not yet completely hostile, there’s a very real possibility that my Father could report him as a criminal running amok in the country to turn them against him. We should also consider the possibility that they might kill Ren’s allies, just as they did with Itsuki last time.

Come to think of it, looking back over the past month, the aggressive actions of the group resembling the Three Heroes Church have gone quiet. It’s safe to assume that clumsy attacks would backfire, and that the Queen’s secret support is having an effect. Trash is also being pushed into a corner due to his position. In that case, there’s no change in what we need to do.
